title: A whale strands below the southern Seann Dunn
summary: A whale comes ashore in an autumn gale below the southern Seann Dunn, stranded beyond the tide's reach. It lives through a day and a night before its breathing stops, watched from a careful distance by the household nearest the shingle who first heard the surf change its voice.

title: The whale cut and shared along the shore
summary: Word of the stranding carries both ways along the shore, and households beyond the one that found it come down to Seann Dunn to help with the cutting. The meat is salted and smoked, the blubber rendered in clay-lined pits, and no household that helped goes home with an empty basket.

title: The whale's ribs driven upright for house frames
summary: Once the meat and the blubber are taken, the whale's bared ribs are driven upright in the turf above the shingle and lashed together at the crown. Three round houses stand roofed in turf by the year's end, taller and wider than any frame of bent branch the shore had raised before.

title: The first rib found cracked through
summary: A rib bearing the heaviest weight of turf is found cracked through in its fifth winter, salt and rain having told on the bone faster than they tell on green wood. It is shored with a driven stake lashed alongside it rather than taken down before the roof can fall.

title: The whale-rib houses raised a second time
summary: The original ribs having failed past shoring, the three houses at Seann Dunn are raised again, this time on bone from a second, smaller stranding that had come ashore some way along the same stretch in the years between, cut by a household with no thought then of building.

title: A child turns up the buried foot of the first rib
summary: Digging in ground long since grown thick with turf, a child of the household turns up a length of bone gone soft and dark with years, and cannot say what it is until an elder names it: the foot of a rib from the first whale-rib house, sunk and near forgotten.

title: The eastern Seann Vell's first dry-stone round house
summary: On ground thick with loose slabs above the eastern Seann Vell, a household raises the first of what will become fourteen round houses, dry stone laid without mortar, each course fitted and refitted until it holds by its own weight alone, roofed at last by corbelled slabs closed with turf.

title: A hearth sunk below the sunk floor at eastern Vell
summary: A household of the eastern Seann Vell cuts its hearth-pit deeper than the sunk floor around it and lines it with stone set on edge, keeping the fire below any draught the door might let in, and letting the smoke find its own way out past the corbelled roof's crown.

title: The first drain cut beneath a wall at eastern Vell
summary: A household whose floor stands wetter than its neighbours' through a wet winter takes up its own floor the following dry season and cuts a stone-lined channel under the wall to carry the water clear. Other households of the cluster, watching, take up their own floors in turn.

title: The fourteenth house finished at eastern Vell
summary: The last of the fourteen round houses stands finished on the eastern Seann Vell's cleared ground, doors facing every way the ground allows, and every house of the cluster by now given its own dry outfall beneath the wall, a drier floor than the cluster's first years knew.

title: A hollow-walled tower begun at the north-western Seann Skell
summary: A household of the north-western Seann Skell, settled where the ground runs out to open water on three sides, begins a round tower of two dry-stone faces built together, a stair let into the gap between them, climbing the wall's own thickness rather than crossing any open floor.

title: A winter storm throws down the unfinished outer face
summary: With the tower a third of its final height, a winter storm throws down the outer face of the stair while the inner holds. The household clears the fallen stone from the gap and sets the cross-stones binding the two faces closer together through the whole climb of what remains to be built.

title: The first night at the tower's crown
summary: With the stair whole and the parapet laid, a household of the north-western Seann Skell climbs to the tower's open crown by clear starlight and sees more of the sea at once than any of that shore had seen from any roof or headland before it.

title: A fire lit on the parapet turns a boat from the rocks
summary: In hard weather, a boat not of that shore is seen from the tower's crown standing in blind toward the rocks below. A fire lit on the parapet shows its crew the coast they are running for in time to bear off from the worst of it before the light fails.

title: Stone huts built in the dune's lee at Seann Toll
summary: A household of Seann Toll builds a row of low stone huts against the slope of a dune tall enough to break the worst of the sea wind before it reaches a wall, turf-roofed and set close, the sand that blows loose in an ordinary gale cleared each morning as an ordinary chore.

title: A wind rises off the sea that does not settle
summary: A wind rises off the sea and holds through a full day and into a second, driving sand off the dune's whole face until the air itself thickens to the colour and near the weight of the ground it carries, and sand mounts against the huts faster than hands can clear it.

title: The household of Seann Toll leaves the buried huts
summary: Before the storm's second night closes on them, the household carries what it can and goes inland to higher ground, none of them lost or badly hurt in the leaving. The dune moves forward the width of the huts and beyond, and the row is not seen again above the sand.

title: New walls raised inland from the buried row
summary: After digging finds the buried huts still whole but past any hope of clearing, the household of Seann Toll gives up the digging and raises new walls further inland, on ground it judges, by the coast's own long habit of wind and sand, unlikely to be claimed again in its own lifetime.
